subject: For nonrecursive observed-variable model, can one specify a correlation between an exogenous and endogenous variable?

messages.author: fd248aedd6f929a2
messages.subject: For nonrecursive observed-variable model, can one specify a correlation between an exogenous and endogenous variable?
parts:
I am not aware of a matrix that represents covariances between  x and xi/ksi variables, but don't know the innards of lavaan. I think LISREL permitted such relationships by using a hidden latent variable model behind observed-variable models, but that is from a long time ago.

Any ideas, techniques or tricks. 

Thanks,

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: For nonrecursive observed-variable model, can one specify a correlation between an exogenous and endogenous variable?
parts:
James,
  I think you may be remembering the method to correlate an observed variable with a latent variable.  Two observed variables are less complicated.

  Lavaan uses the LISREL all-Y representation, as does Mplus.  As such, endogenous and exogenous variables are all in the same matrices because they are all parameterized in LISREL's matrices for endogenous variables.

  You can directly specify a covariance between the residuals of an exogenous and endogenous observed variable as a free parameter.

# A Holzinger and Swineford (1939) example
HS.model <- '
  x1 ~ x2
  x2 ~ x3
  x1 ~~ x3  #covariance between exogenous x3 and endogenous x1
  x1~~x1
  x2~~x2
  x3~~x3
  ' # end model

fit <- lavaan(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(fit, fit.measures=TRUE)




However, if you meant that you wanted to fix the correlation between two such variables, that will be a function of the paths in the model.  So, you would have to work through the correlation as a function of those parameters.

Also, remember that bow patterns are not statistically identified.  Two parameters for one covariance produce a singularity.

Keith
